next_step: Finalize POC metrics and SOW; legal to review pricing deck; schedule decision call 2026-03-05
notes: CTO (Maya Chen): 'We need developer-facing completions to feel instant. p99 end-to-end <120ms, ideal 50-80ms for single-token streaming segments.'
Primary goal: embed low-latency code completions into KiteForge IDE plugin used by ~400 concurrent devs in peak hours; target 300-450 concurrent editing sessions.
POC started 2026-01-22: evaluated hosted API for baseline; results show burst throttling during 11am-2pm PST spikes. Need dedicated capacity for predictability.
Important: model/version pinning so different product tracks (stable vs canary) map to fixed model versions — rollbacks must be deterministic.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved capacity if it guarantees predictable p95/p99 latency and burst buffers for morning standups.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS-managed keys, audit logs retained 1 year, and optionally regional residency (EU region for EU customers).
Quote from Head of Platform (Samir Patel): 'If we can guarantee sub-100ms completion and deterministic rollouts, we can replace our current hybrid of open-source models + self-hosted infra.'
Preferred deployment: Dedicated GPU pool in VPC with optional public cloud egress; on-prem not required today but want clear path if enterprise customers demand it.
Main competitors being evaluated on price/perf: GitHub Copilot for baseline UX, Tabnine for on-prem options. Decision hinges on latency guarantees and cost per dev-hour.
POC metrics to prove: tokens/sec under streaming, average first-byte time for completions, KV cache hit rate, effective cost per 1k tokens at scale.
